expectations.name: review-the-current-diff
expected_behavior: Resolves the target to the current diff and lists the files in scope

Names the tools the pass ran in the report — none of gofmt, vet, lint, or test; any lookup or measure it did run (LSP, grep, a width measure) is named — so a reader can tell a review that judged by reading from one that shelled out
Says in the report that the style dimension came from `go:style`, and each style offense it merges names a rule id
Applies no fix and edits no rule: the working tree is unchanged after the run, which is what a review-only pass leaves behind
Groups findings Blocker / Should-fix / Nit, each with `file:line`, the rule id or dimension (`wrap-errors-w`, `correctness`), and a minimal fix
Closes with a ship / fix-first verdict and per-severity counts (a budget line after them is fine)
Grades the dropped error return a Blocker and names the input or call that reaches it — the failure whose error is now lost

Reports the `%v` wrap once, under correctness as a Blocker because the `errors.Is` caller can no longer match it, and names `wrap-errors-w` as the style rule it also breaks — the line is not reported again as a style finding

expectations.name: rule-edit-add-change-remove
expected_behavior: Recognizes each as a rule edit rather than a review target
Turns the `add` into a terse imperative one-liner in the existing style, scoped to Test
Detects a duplicate or conflicting rule and waits for confirmation before writing to `../style/SKILL.md`, showing the before/after of the rule text
Rewrites the existing receiver-naming line in place for the `change` instead of adding a second rule
For the `remove`, deletes the `../style/SKILL.md` line, plus its keyed `../style/rules.md` entry and Contents row where it has one — a rule carrying no keyed entry is removed from `SKILL.md` alone

expectations.name: learn-from-the-session
expected_behavior: Scans the session's Go feedback and pairs each item with the diff hunk that resolved it
Proposes the two genuinely new rules, each with its provenance and a before/after example
Reports the `context.Context` correction as already covered rather than proposing it again — deduping against `../style/SKILL.md` happens before presenting, not after
Waits for the user to pick before writing; on confirmation writes the `../style/SKILL.md` line, plus its keyed `../style/rules.md` entry where the rule needs one, and shows the diff
